findings.reason: the node implementing §23 must either re-key the claim on the group (contradicting the key the plan states) or extend the lift row in `lift_watch.py` outside its write paths, and none of the done-when's cases distinguish a group-keyed claim from an id-keyed one, so the gate passes either way and the discrepancy survives to the built code.
findings.text: §23 states the session's followers "share one claim per (session, lift id, transition)", yet the same paragraph notes the row carries "the group is in `node`" with `run_id` `None`; `_lift_row` in `reckon/crew/lift_watch.py:192-204` sets `node` to the lift's **group** and places the lift **id** only inside the `detail` free-text clause ("…, id 'codex-sub-1792002586-64d825'"), which §20 removed from the rendered row, and §17's `_feed_lift` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:1680) likewise reads the group from `node`. So the follower has no structured lift id to key a claim on, and the only module that could add one (`lift_watch.py`) is not among §23's declared write paths (ticker.py, crew_follow_commands.py, and the new test).
